drugs.name: Aglepristone
drugs.indication: Pregnancy termination where clinically appropriate
drugs.notes: Confirm pregnancy/termination where possible and use cascade consent.

drugs.name: Aglepristone
drugs.indication: Pyometra/metritis support where progesterone blockade is selected
drugs.notes: Use with reproductive diagnosis and close monitoring.

drugs.name: Aglepristone
drugs.indication: Pregnancy termination where clinically appropriate
drugs.notes: Specialist/reproductive judgement required.

drugs.name: Asparaginase
drugs.indication: Lymphoid malignancy protocol component
drugs.frequency: Weekly for first 3 weeks as protocol directs
drugs.notes: Cytotoxic/oncology protocol drug. Not suitable for mg/kg calculator.

drugs.name: Asparaginase
drugs.indication: Lymphoid leukaemia/lymphoma protocol component
drugs.notes: Cytotoxic/oncology protocol drug. Not suitable for mg/kg calculator.

drugs.name: Dinoprostone
drugs.indication: Egg binding support by cloacal/vaginal relaxation
drugs.notes: Topical gel row; not suitable for mg/kg calculator.

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine
drugs.indication: Allergic reactions or vaccine-reaction prophylaxis
drugs.frequency: q8-12h; IM high end before vaccination where indicated
drugs.notes: Liquid may be unpalatable; monitor sedation.

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine
drugs.indication: Torticollis-associated nausea/motion sickness support
drugs.notes: Use as adjunct while underlying vestibular disease is addressed.

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine
drugs.indication: Allergic reaction/pruritus support
drugs.frequency: q12h or as required by species
drugs.notes: Use lower end in small/debilitated patients.

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine
drugs.indication: Allergic rhinitis, hypersensitivity or allergic dermatopathy support
drugs.notes: Monitor for hypotension and sedation.

drugs.name: Finasteride
drugs.indication: Benign prostatic hyperplasia associated with adrenal gland disease
drugs.notes: Do not use in breeding ferrets; human pregnancy handling precautions.

drugs.name: Hydralazine
drugs.indication: Afterload reduction / hypertension support where selected
drugs.notes: Hospital monitoring recommended due to hypotension risk.
drugs.formulation: Injectable powder for reconstitution; oral tablets

drugs.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
drugs.indication: Adjunct diuretic for refractory fluid overload or calcium oxalate prevention
drugs.notes: Use with renal/electrolyte monitoring; avoid renal impairment.

drugs.name: Hydroxyzine
drugs.indication: Pruritus/allergic disease support
drugs.notes: May cause sedation and may reduce seizure threshold.
drugs.formulation: Oral 10 mg/25 mg tablets; 2 mg/ml syrup

drugs.name: Hydroxyzine
drugs.indication: Pruritus/allergic disease support
drugs.notes: Use with caution in urinary retention, glaucoma or pyloroduodenal obstruction.
drugs.formulation: Oral 10 mg/25 mg tablets; 2 mg/ml syrup

drugs.name: Hydroxyzine
drugs.indication: Feather plucking/pruritus support where allergic component suspected
drugs.notes: Use only after husbandry, behavioural and infectious causes are considered.
drugs.formulation: Oral 10 mg/25 mg tablets; 2 mg/ml syrup

drugs.name: Latanoprost
drugs.indication: Primary glaucoma / acute intraocular pressure reduction
drugs.notes: Topical ophthalmic row; not suitable for mg/kg calculator.

drugs.name: Milbemycin oxime
drugs.indication: Nematode control / heartworm prevention where regionally appropriate
drugs.notes: Do not use in animals suspected of heartworm disease; avoid under 0.5 kg.
drugs.formulation: Oral tablets in combination products vary

drugs.name: Nitenpyram
drugs.indication: Flea treatment / flystrike support where appropriate
drugs.notes: Use as part of integrated parasite control.

drugs.name: Prazosin
drugs.indication: Urethral smooth muscle relaxation / functional urethral obstruction support
drugs.notes: Monitor for first-dose hypotension, weakness and syncope.
drugs.formulation: Oral 0.5 mg, 1 mg, 2 mg, 5 mg tablets

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.indication: Anti-inflammatory therapy or lymphoma/adrenalectomy protocol support
drugs.notes: Use lowest effective dose and taper after chronic therapy.

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.indication: Short anti-inflammatory course where benefits outweigh risks
drugs.notes: Rabbits are sensitive to steroids; use carefully and avoid infectious disease masking.

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.indication: Pruritus/inflammatory disease after infectious causes excluded
drugs.notes: Exclude aspergillosis, chlamydiosis and other infections before use.

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.indication: Anti-inflammatory therapy or oncology protocol support
drugs.notes: Use cautiously; immunosuppression and infection risk are important.

drugs.name: Proligestone
drugs.indication: Prevention of prolonged oestrus complications
drugs.frequency: 50 mg/ferret, then 25 mg after 7 days if needed
drugs.notes: Fixed-dose row; not suitable for mg/kg calculator. Authorized in ferrets.

drugs.name: Proligestone
drugs.indication: False pregnancy treatment/prevention
drugs.notes: Avoid in diabetic animals; do not use in birds.

drugs.name: Propentofylline
drugs.indication: Raptor wing-tip oedema / pododermatitis support / cognitive dysfunction support
drugs.notes: Anecdotal avian use; monitor cardiovascular tolerance.

drugs.name: Rifampicin
drugs.indication: Combination therapy for selected staphylococcal osteomyelitis/mycobacterial-type infections
drugs.notes: EMA Avoid category. Do not use as monotherapy because resistance develops readily.

drugs.name: Rifampicin
drugs.indication: Combination therapy for selected mycobacterial/chlamydial-type infections
drugs.notes: Use only with culture/diagnostics and combination protocol rationale.

drugs.name: Sotalol
drugs.indication: Arrhythmia management where beta-blockade/class III effect is selected
drugs.notes: Specialist/cardiology use; monitor heart rate and rhythm.

drugs.name: Spironolactone
drugs.indication: Adjunct therapy for congestive heart failure / aldosterone antagonism
drugs.notes: Monitor potassium, renal values and hydration.

drugs.name: Spironolactone
drugs.indication: Adjunct therapy for congestive heart failure / aldosterone antagonism
drugs.notes: Use with ACE inhibitor/diuretic plans only with monitoring.

drugs.name: Tetracaine
drugs.indication: Single-application ocular surface anaesthesia
drugs.notes: Topical anaesthetic; not for therapeutic use and not suitable for calculator.

drugs.name: Theophylline
drugs.indication: Small airway disease / bronchodilation support
drugs.notes: Low therapeutic index; dose on lean bodyweight and monitor toxicity.

drugs.name: Theophylline
drugs.indication: Small airway disease / bronchodilation support
drugs.notes: Low therapeutic index; monitor cardiovascular/CNS signs.

drugs.name: Theophylline
drugs.indication: Bronchodilation support
drugs.notes: Monitor for excitation, tachycardia and seizures.

drugs.name: Thiamazole
drugs.indication: Hyperthyroidism control
drugs.notes: Monitor T4, CBC, biochemistry and renal values.

drugs.name: Thiamazole
drugs.indication: Hyperthyroidism control
drugs.notes: Monitor clinical response; specialist reptile endocrinology case.

drugs.name: Tricaine methanesulfonate
drugs.indication: Fish anaesthesia or euthanasia by immersion
drugs.frequency: Induction; maintain at lower concentration as needed
drugs.notes: Bath/immersion row; not suitable for mg/kg calculator. Buffer and monitor water quality.

drugs.name: Vincristine
drugs.indication: Lymphoma chemotherapy protocol component
drugs.notes: Cytotoxic vesicant; give via secure IV catheter only.

drugs.name: Vincristine
drugs.indication: Selected lymphoma/oncology protocol component
drugs.notes: Specialist oncology use only.

drugs.name: Vincristine
drugs.indication: Selected lymphoma protocol component
drugs.notes: Case-report level evidence; specialist oncology use only.

drugs.name: Xylazine
drugs.indication: Sedation or ketamine-combination anaesthesia
drugs.notes: Largely superseded by medetomidine/dexmedetomidine; cardiovascular risk.

drugs.name: Xylazine
drugs.indication: Sedation / ketamine-combination anaesthesia
drugs.notes: Avoid cardiovascular or systemic disease.

drugs.name: Xylazine
drugs.indication: Analgesic effect reported in Xenopus/leopard frog models
drugs.notes: Specialist amphibian use; monitor carefully.

information.content: Progesterone receptor antagonist used for selected reproductive indications such as pregnancy termination and pyometra/metritis support in exotic mammals.
People who are or may become pregnant should not handle it; use caution in diabetes or suspected hypoadrenocorticism.
Cytotoxic enzyme used as part of lymphoma or lymphoid leukaemia protocols in selected exotic species.
Cytotoxic handling precautions apply and anaphylaxis risk increases with repeated doses.
Prostaglandin E2 preparation used topically to support cloacal/vaginal relaxation in egg-bound birds.
People who are or may become pregnant and asthmatics should avoid handling; uterine rupture is a concern.
H1 antihistamine used for allergic reactions, vaccine-reaction prophylaxis and selected vestibular/nausea situations.
Avoid or use caution in urinary retention, glaucoma and hyperthyroidism; sedation can combine with other CNS depressants.
5-alpha reductase inhibitor used for prostatic enlargement associated with adrenal disease in ferrets.
Do not use in breeding ferrets; human pregnancy handling precautions are important.
Arteriolar vasodilator/afterload reducer used only with close cardiovascular monitoring.
Can cause severe hypotension and reflex tachycardia, so hospital monitoring is recommended.
Thiazide diuretic used as adjunctive therapy for selected refractory fluid overload or urolith prevention cases.
Avoid renal impairment and monitor electrolytes because hypokalaemia and volume contraction can develop.
H1 antihistamine sometimes used for pruritus or feather-plucking support after underlying causes are addressed.
May cause sedation and reduce seizure threshold; use only after investigating underlying pruritus/behaviour causes.
Topical prostaglandin analogue used to reduce intraocular pressure in glaucoma.
Avoid in uveitis and anterior lens luxation; ocular irritation and miosis can occur.
Macrocyclic lactone antiparasitic used for nematode control and regional heartworm prevention in ferrets.
Do not use in animals suspected of heartworm disease or under 0.5 kg.
Rapid oral flea adulticide used as part of integrated parasite control and sometimes flystrike support.
Only kills adult fleas present at dosing; environmental and household control remain essential.
Alpha-1 antagonist used to relax urethral smooth muscle and support selected functional obstruction cases.
First-dose hypotension and syncope can occur, especially with diuretics or beta-blockers.
Systemic or topical glucocorticoid used for inflammatory, immune-mediated and oncology indications when benefits outweigh risks.
Avoid in pregnancy, diabetes, renal disease and ulcerative keratitis; rabbits are particularly steroid-sensitive.
Long-acting progestagen used for prolonged oestrus prevention in ferrets and selected rabbit pseudopregnancy cases.
Avoid diabetic animals and do not use in birds; long-term progestagen effects can be significant.
Xanthine derivative used anecdotally in birds for vascular and pododermatitis-related indications.
May increase myocardial oxygen demand; evidence is limited and mostly anecdotal in birds.
Rifamycin antibiotic used only in carefully justified combination protocols because resistance develops quickly.
EMA Avoid category; use only in combination and avoid pregnancy or liver disease.
Beta-blocking/class III antiarrhythmic used for selected avian arrhythmia cases under specialist judgement.
Avoid bradyarrhythmia and decompensated heart failure; ECG/heart-rate monitoring is important.
Aldosterone antagonist and potassium-sparing diuretic used as adjunctive cardiology therapy.
Monitor potassium and renal values, especially with ACE inhibitors or renal compromise.
Topical ocular local anaesthetic for single diagnostic use only.
Do not use therapeutically; topical anaesthetics delay corneal epithelial healing.
Methylxanthine bronchodilator with a low therapeutic index used for selected airway disease cases.
Low therapeutic index; arrhythmias, seizures and GI signs indicate possible toxicity.
Antithyroid drug used for hyperthyroidism control in selected exotic patients.
Do not use in pregnancy/lactation; monitor CBC, biochemistry, T4 and renal values.
Buffered immersion anaesthetic for fish, also used at higher concentration for euthanasia protocols.
Solutions must be buffered and tested in a small group before treating many fish.
Cytotoxic vinca alkaloid used in specialist lymphoma/oncology protocols.
Vesicant cytotoxic drug; extravasation can cause severe tissue injury.
Alpha-2 agonist sedative/analgesic largely superseded by medetomidine and dexmedetomidine because of cardiovascular effects.
Do not use in cardiovascular/systemic disease, pregnancy or diabetics; birds/reptiles no longer recommended.

Active pancreatitis, history of pancreatitis or previous asparaginase-associated anaphylaxis.
Use without ability to monitor or where reproductive tract rupture risk is unacceptable.
Hypovolaemia, hypotension, renal impairment or cerebral bleeding.
Renal impairment or uncontrolled electrolyte disturbance.
Suspected heartworm disease or bodyweight below 0.5 kg.

Bradyarrhythmias or acute/decompensated congestive heart failure.
Cardiovascular/systemic disease, pregnancy, diabetes or situations where vomiting is contraindicated.

species_warnings.warning: Rabbits are highly sensitive to corticosteroids, including topical preparations.
Exclude infectious causes such as aspergillosis or chlamydiosis before steroid use.
No longer recommended because safer alpha-2 options are available.
Topical ocular anaesthetics delay corneal healing and should not be used therapeutically.
Use only in combination protocols; resistance emerges readily.
Low therapeutic index. Monitor for tremors, tachycardia, arrhythmias and seizures.
Cytotoxic vesicant. Secure IV access and chemotherapy handling precautions are essential.
Use only with reproductive assessment; uterine/oviduct rupture is a concern.
Buffer solutions and test a small group before treating large numbers.
Avoid with uveitis or anterior lens luxation; monitor ocular comfort.
Monitor potassium and renal values if combined with ACE inhibitors.
Monitor haematology, liver/renal values and thyroid response.
Use as part of an oncology protocol with cytotoxic precautions.
Avoid animals suspected of heartworm disease and those under 0.5 kg.
First dose hypotension can occur; start with monitoring.

interactions.mechanism: Potent enzyme induction can reduce azole exposure.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid or monitor response and adjust with specialist guidance.
interactions.interaction: Avoid or monitor response and adjust with specialist guidance.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin may increase metabolism of barbiturates.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor seizure control and drug levels where possible.
interactions.interaction: Monitor seizure control and drug levels where possible.

interactions.mechanism: Fluoroquinolones can increase theophylline concentrations.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid if possible or monitor for toxicity.
interactions.interaction: Avoid if possible or monitor for toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Cimetidine may increase theophylline concentrations.
Combination may increase seizure risk.
interactions.recommendation: Use caution, especially in seizure-prone patients.
interactions.interaction: Use caution, especially in seizure-prone patients.

interactions.mechanism: Additive negative chronotropy and AV conduction effects.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid or monitor ECG/heart rate closely.
interactions.interaction: Avoid or monitor ECG/heart rate closely.

interactions.mechanism: Combined therapy may increase potassium and renal risk.
Additive diuresis and hypokalaemia risk.
Thiazide-induced hypokalaemia can increase digoxin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor potassium and digoxin toxicity signs.
interactions.interaction: Monitor potassium and digoxin toxicity signs.

interactions.mechanism: Additive GI ulceration and renal/perfusion risk.
Glucocorticoids can antagonize insulin effects.
Asparaginase can reduce vincristine clearance if sequencing is wrong.
interactions.recommendation: Give vincristine 12-24h before asparaginase when used together.
interactions.interaction: Give vincristine 12-24h before asparaginase when used together.

interactions.mechanism: CYP inhibition may increase vincristine exposure.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid or use oncology specialist guidance.
interactions.interaction: Avoid or use oncology specialist guidance.

interactions.mechanism: Additive sedation.
interactions.recommendation: Use reduced sedative dosing and monitor.
interactions.interaction: Use reduced sedative dosing and monitor.

interactions.mechanism: Increased first-dose hypotension risk.
Incompatibility/irritation concern.
Topical anaesthetics block reflex tearing.
interactions.recommendation: Perform Schirmer testing before anaesthetic application.
interactions.interaction: Perform Schirmer testing before anaesthetic application.

interactions.mechanism: Alpha-2 effects and myocardial sensitization increase cardiovascular risk.
Phenobarbital may reduce antithyroid clinical effect.
Reduced hepatic oxidation may increase thiamazole concentrations.
P-glycoprotein effects may increase macrocyclic lactone CNS exposure.
Acidic solutions increase stress and toxicity risk.
